page: Google Cloud Platform a4x-highgpu-4g is an accelerator-optimized instance within the GPU Machines family. Built on the arm64 CPU architecture, it provides 140 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 884.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 6.31 GB of RAM per core. This configuration balances high host compute capacity with large memory pools to manage preprocessing pipelines and large in-memory tensors.

Acceleration is powered by four NVIDIA GB200 GPUs from the Blackwell family, offering a combined 744 GB of GPU video memory. To address high-throughput local disk I/O demands, the machine bundles 12885 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly on the host. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking configurations for ingress and egress routing.

The combination of 744 GB total VRAM, dedicated arm64 compute cores, and high-capacity local NVMe storage targets workloads requiring massive parallel processing and rapid checkpointing. The system profile is tailored for large-scale artificial intelligence model training, high-parameter LLM inference, scientific simulations, and distributed deep learning pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform a4x-highgpu-4g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine belonging to the GPU Machines family. Designed for compute-heavy and machine learning workloads, it integrates 140 dedicated arm64 vCPUs with 884.0 GB of system memory, averaging 6.31 GB per vCPU. The instance is equipped with four NVIDIA GB200 Blackwell GPUs delivering an aggregate of 744 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM, facilitating massive model parallelization. In addition to high-density host memory and GPU capacity, the server bundles 12885 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage for intensive local data caching and scratch space. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. This resource distribution makes the instance suited for large language model pre-training, complex distributed deep learning workloads, high-throughput model inference, and data-intensive accelerator-driven simulations.
